scope: Original PLY-1 precise finite Split component diagnostic and local-test correction; no native comparison
observations: The topology analyzer reports 31 source components and four degenerate triangles. It skips those zero-area triangles while building edge adjacency, leaving each as a singleton component.

Split's compact edge grouping retains the four zero-area faces and reports 27 source groups. The precise Split returns 30 parts; two large parts contain the four retained zero-area facets and their indexed edge neighbors.
The unchanged baseline and the source-coverage candidate produced byte-identical complete diagnostic receipts, including all output segment hashes, part sizes, source hashes and area.
All 30 resulting parts lie on one side of the cutter within 1e-6 mm and both sides are represented.
testCorrection: The generic original-file test now checks per-part sidedness and representation of both sides. The previously intended two-part assertion remains for the pinned PLY-3 SHA-256, rather than assuming every input is one component.
limitations: Input component definitions differ: topology diagnostics exclude degenerate faces from adjacency, while Split grouping uses all indexed edges.
Sidedness, area and matching baseline output do not establish native Split equivalence or full GUI/MCP lifecycle for PLY-1.
The M2 native and milestone acceptance gates remain open.
